title: Terraform observability module: simulative upgrade runbook, drift detector, and zero-downtime Grafana provisioning
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Scope: Build a safe, repeatable upgrade path and validation harness for the Terraform observability module that manages Prometheus + Grafana + OpenTelemetry Collector + log shipping. The goal is zero-downtime provisioning for Grafana dashboards and datasource changes, automated detection of terraform drift in VPC environments, and a deterministic staged rollout that can be simulated before touching customer VPCs.

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Provide a documented runbook that lets SREs run a simulated module upgrade against a sandbox VPC and validate outcome in < 2 hours.
- Implement a lightweight drift detector (Lambda + TF plan watcher) that flags resource drift with a reproducible plan link in Slack and the Console.
- Ensure Grafana provisioning changes are applied without dashboard downtime: use blue/green provisioning by creating temporary organizations and swapping datasource IDs in a single transaction where supported.
- Ensure Prometheus recording and alerting rule migrations run with non-destructive verification (dry-run of rule evals against a replayed scrape) before applying.
- Add Terratest/pytest harness that runs `terraform plan` and an apply in a disposable sandbox, then runs an automated test suite: scrape validation, OTLP ingest smoke tests, and log shipping end-to-end.
- Provide automatic rollback hooks (terraform destroy or tfstate restore) and a clearly enumerated manual rollback procedure in the runbook.

Design proposals and trade-offs considered:
- Drift detector design: serverless (Lambda) vs controller (K8s operator). Chosen: Lambda for minimal runtime overhead and ease of running in customer VPCs without adding cluster-level components. Trade-off: operator would offer richer reconciliation but increases user surface area.
- Grafana zero-downtime: we evaluated in-place dashboard updates vs blue/green provisioning. Blue/green requires temporary storage and a single atomic swap but adds complexity to provisioning code. We will implement an optional blue/green mode behind a module flag `grafana_zero_downtime = true`.
- Prometheus rule migration: instead of attempting in-flight rewriting of rules, we will perform a canary evaluation using a replayed scrape dataset in the sandbox, then promote rules to production. This avoids transient alert storms but requires maintaining a short-term replay store for the test harness.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Runbook + design doc (Confluence) + checklist for SREs. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Observability+Upgrade+Runbook
2) Drift detector Lambda: publish 1.0 as TF module optional resource with SNS/Slack alerting, store plan artifacts in customer S3 prefix. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3456
3) Terratest harness repo and CI jobs that spin ephemeral sandbox accounts/VPCs for upgrade rehearsals. Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-upgrade-harness
4) Grafana blue/green provisioning implementation in module with migration scripts and atomic swap logic; include migration tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/1222
5) Prometheus alert rule dry-run tooling and migration scripts; include a replay store in the harness. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/alert-rules-migrator/pull/48
6) Release the module changes behind a major version bump and publish release notes + automated guidance in Console and docs.

Rollout strategy:
- Phase 0: Internal rehearsals in the `obs-upgrade-harness` sandbox; iterate until test pass rate >= 95%.
- Phase 1: Invite 2 low-risk internal customers to opt into a staged upgrade (canary). Monitor SLOs for 48 hours.
- Phase 2: Gradual ramp across Dedicated instances with automatic pause on increased error budget consumption.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests for Terraform modules (tfsdk) and Go/Python helpers.
- Integration tests in harness: OTLP ingest smoke, scrape validation, alert firing simulation, log ingestion to S3/Kinesis.
- Post-upgrade automated checks: prometheus rule sanity, grafana API health, otel-collector pipeline throughput smoke.

Monitoring and observability for upgrades:
- Add a temporary upgrade dashboard that tracks `tf_apply_duration`, `plan_drift_detected`, `grafana_swap_time_ms`, `alert_firing_rate` and `otel_pipeline_errors`. Dashboard link (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/upgrade/observability-upgrades

Rollback and incident playbook:
- Automatic rollback triggers: failed smoke tests post-apply, alert storm > threshold, increase in 5xx > 3x baseline.
- Manual rollback steps documented in runbook, with explicit tfstate restore commands and cluster-level restart steps for collector pods.

Security and compliance notes:
- Plan artifacts and drift diffs will be stored in customer S3 prefixes encrypted with customer KMS keys.
- Module changes that touch IAM roles or cross-account resources will require pre-approval and a security sign-off (security_review_required).

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Do we accept the additional cost/maintenance of the replay store for rule dry-runs, or keep dry-runs limited to synthetic traffic generators?
- Should the drift detector run on a fixed cadence (24h) or be event-driven (TF apply webhook + periodic)? Recommendation: hybrid (event-driven for immediate plans + nightly full sweep).

Deliverables:
- TF module changes merged and tagged v2.0.0 (observability-2026.03).
- obs-upgrade-harness repo with CI jobs and sandbox repro.
- Runbook on Confluence and a Console-guided upgrade checklist.

Acceptance criteria checklist (must all pass):
- [ ] Harness runs a simulated upgrade and validates OTLP, Prometheus scrape, and log shipping without regressions.
- [ ] Drift detector generates reproducible plan artifacts and a linked alert in Slack.
- [ ] Grafana provisioning zero-downtime flag successfully swaps dashboards in internal canary.
- [ ] Prometheus rule migrations validated in replay and safely promoted.

Notes: This ticket focuses on the infrastructure and automation for safe upgrades; follow-up tickets will address UX flows in Console and formal enterprise rollout sign-up mechanics.
